title: Pietro e la sua pizzeria
summary: Week 4 review and immersion: Pietro's Naples routine and his favorite pizzeria.

blocks.title: Una settimana a tavola
blocks.body: This week: meal structure (*colazione, pranzo, cena, il primo, il secondo*), ordering with **vorrei / per me / mi porta… / il conto**, the modal engine **potere/volere/dovere**, the *piacere* trap (**mi piace** vs **mi piacciono**), and market quantities (*un etto, un chilo*). Time to put it all in one native voice.
blocks.callout: Everything below uses this week's targets — read for the story, then check what you caught.

blocks.prompt: How do you say 'I like tortellini' (i tortellini, plural)?
blocks.explain: *Tortellini* is plural, so it's *mi piacciono* — the verb agrees with what's liked.

pairs.left: *vorrei* — a polite wish: *vorrei provare la pizza*
pairs.note: Both pair with a plain infinitive — the modal engine from this week.

blocks.explain: *Un chilo di pomodori* — quantity + di + the thing, same pattern as at the market.

blocks.scene: Pietro tells you about his daily routine in Naples and his favorite neighborhood pizzeria

lines.speaker: Pietro
lines.target: Allora, qui a Napoli la giornata comincia presto: un caffè al banco, in piedi, due chiacchiere col barista.
lines.en: So, here in Naples the day starts early: a coffee at the counter, standing, a quick chat with the barista.

lines.speaker: Pietro
lines.target: Dopo il lavoro, la sera, vado quasi sempre nella stessa pizzeria — la stessa famiglia la gestisce da trent'anni.
lines.en: After work, in the evening, I almost always go to the same pizzeria — the same family has run it for thirty years.

lines.speaker: Pietro
lines.target: Una margherita, sempre. Qui diciamo che la vera pizza si mangia solo a Napoli.
lines.en: A margherita, always. Here we say real pizza can only be eaten in Naples.
lines.spotlight: Southern pride, said with a smile — not aggressive, just certain.

lines.speaker: Pietro
lines.target: A casa, con mia moglie e mia figlia, a volte parliamo napoletano — ma con te parlo sempre in italiano standard.
lines.en: At home, with my wife and daughter, we sometimes speak Neapolitan — but with you I always speak standard Italian.
lines.spotlight: Pietro code-switches with family but keeps standard Italian with you — dialect is real, just not what we teach.

lines.speaker: You
lines.target: Posso venire con te alla pizzeria, una sera?
lines.en: Can I come with you to the pizzeria one evening?

lines.speaker: Pietro
lines.target: Certo! Sono sicuro che ti piace — è meglio della pizza del nord, te lo dico io.
lines.en: Of course! I'm sure you'll like it — it's better than pizza from the north, I'm telling you.
lines.spotlight: A gentle jab at the north — classic Pietro.

questions.q: Where does Pietro have his coffee in the morning?
options: Standing at the counter of a bar
